title: SIFTER: Electrophoretic complex fractionation protocol
protocol: Prepare the stock buffer solutions for F-actin Stabilization Buffer and F-actin depolymerization Buffer.
Titrate the F-actin Stabilization Buffer to pH = 7.4 by adding 1.1% HCl (or similar).
Store the buffers at 4°C when not in use.
Prepare gel precursor solution (10 mL) and degas for several minutes.
Treat glass plates with 1 mL of GelSlick solution and dry with KimWipe.
Place spacers between the two glass plates.
Pipette entire 10 mL gel precursor solution between the plates.
Tape an SU-8 mold onto the lab bench to hold in place during processing.
Make the gel precursor solution and degas with a bath sonicator and vacuum line to eliminate bubbles.
Add initiators (APS and TEMED) to gel precursor solution, mix well without forming bubbles.
Pipette a 250 μl droplet near one of the short edges of the SU-8 mold.
Add a silanized slide on top of the droplet slowly to prevent trapping bubbles.
After loading, press gently on the slide to squeeze excess precursor from the gap and ensure the micropillars on the SU-8 mold are in contact with the slide.
Let chemical polymerization proceed for 15 minutes.
Add 1-2 ml of PBS to rehydrate the edge of the slide and facilitate release from the SU-8 mold.
Gently slide a razor blade underneath the slide and lift straight up to detach the gel slide from the SU-8 mold.
Place the PAG slide in a 4-well rectangular slide plate filled with PBS before use, ensuring the side with the PAG layer faces up.
Turn on water bath and set to 75 °C.
Add 12 g of urea to separate 50 mL conical tubes for each separation assay.
Remove 15.9 mL of buffer from the tube containing gel lids in F-actin depolymerization buffer and add it to the 12g urea conical tube to make 25 mL of 1X RIPA + 8M urea.
Put the F-actin depolymerization buffer (1X RIPA + 8M urea) in the water bath to dissolve for ~10 min.
Swirl the conical tubes to assist with dissolving the last of the urea.
Add 25 mL of F-actin stabilization buffer multiplied by the number of separation assays into a glass bottle.
Add 1.95 mg of fresh DTE per 25 mL of buffer and swirl to dissolve.
Remove excess buffer solution from the gel lid conical tubes containing F-actin stabilization buffer and replace with buffer solution containing DTE.
Keep the stabilization gel lids at room temperature after adding DTE.
Attach leads to electrophoresis chamber and set power supply to constant voltage operation mode at 90 V (30 V/cm).
Turn on Hamamatsu UV source lamp and allow it to warm up for 10 minutes.
Set up buffer waste bottles next to the separation station.
Fill a 3 cm dish with 10 mM Tris HCl (pH=7.5).
Situate the custom electrophoresis chamber on top of the PID heating element. Turn on PID controller to heat the top of the custom electrophoresis chamber to 37°C.
Wash dish of cells with 1X PBS.
Trypsinize cells for 3 min at 37 °C.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation.
Resuspend cells in 1X PBS to achieve a concentration ~10^6 cells/mL.
Introduce ~300 uL of cell suspension onto the polyacrylamide gel in microwell device.
Gently move the microwell gel back and forth every few minutes to disperse cells.
Settle for a total of 10 minutes.
Wash excess cells off the surface gently with 1 mL 1X PBS three times.
Submerge EP cytometry microwell gel in the dish of Tris HCl buffer for ~10s.
Add a ~1 mm diameter dab of vaseline to the glass of the EP chamber where you will place the lower left corner of the EP cytometry gel.
Remove the EP cytometry gel from the buffer and dry the back of the slide with a Kimwipe.
Place the gel on the vaseline (glass side down, gel side up) and press down lightly. Ensure the slide is straight (parallel to graphite electrodes).
Select a tube of F-actin stabilization buffer containing a gel lid. Lightly swirl the tube to remove the gel from the walls of the tube.
Pour the buffer into buffer waste and let the gel lid slide to the opening of the tube.
Place the gel lid in contact with the two electrodes and over the surface of the microwell gel.
Lyse cells for 45s.
Turn on the E-field (30 V/cm) for 45-60s (45 for actin, 60 for GFP-actin in a 1-mm separation lane).
Turn off the E-field and turn on the UV source for 45s at 100% power.
Reverse the lead connections to the EP chamber.
Remove the gel lid from the microwell gel.
Retrieve the F-actin depolymerization gel lid buffer tube from the water bath and swirl it prior to pouring its contents into buffer waste, allowing the gel lid to slide to the opening of the tube.
Place the gel lid on the microwell gel and allow depolymerization to proceed for 45 seconds.
Perform electrophoresis for 45-60 seconds at 30 V/cm.
Apply UV light for 45 seconds at 100%.
Remove the microwell gel from the EP chamber and place it in a 4-well dish containing 1X TBST. Wash for at least one hour prior to immunoprobing.
